messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs  Acme Health

Hi Jared 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Great to hear more about Acme Health's use case for chart summarization and patient triage. As promised, I wanted to summarize the key items we discussed around PII and data handling and confirm the next steps so your procurement and security teams can move quickly.

Quick recap (high level):
- What we heard: you need clarity on whether prompts/outputs are stored, retention windows, logging controls, and data residency for the hosted API vs Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Why it matters: PHI/PII exposure risks + contractual requirements for data locality and deletion on request.

Core answers (short form)  full details attached: PII_handling_summary.pdf
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): by default we retain request/response logs for 30 days for debugging/abuse monitoring. Prompts and outputs are not used to train models. With an enterprise contract you can opt out of request/response logging (no-store) or request shorter retention; we can also apply region-specific retention rules (e.g., EU region).
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): logs and request/response data remain within your dedicated environment; retention is controlled by your tenancy and SLA  typically configurable to 0 days for prompts/outputs.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full control  no data is sent to Redwood control plane unless you enable it; retention is managed by your infra.
4) Audit logs & encryption: all persisted data is encrypted at rest (customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private). Audit logs are available via Console and can be retained for 90 days by default; longer retention can be negotiated.

Next steps I propose:
- Send a short written confirmation with the above specifics for your procurement/legal (I attached the one-pager).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our security engineer to cover KMS, HSM, and deletion workflows (30\u201345m).
- If you want a non-prod test in the EU region to validate residency, we can spin up a Dedicated test pool for you next week.

Please let me know which of the above you want in writing and whether proc/legal need any additional artifacts (SOC2, penetration test summary).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer  Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
[Attachment: PII_handling_summary.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

Rishi 

Thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. A few specific questions we need answered in writing for procurement:
1) Are prompts and model outputs persisted by default for Hosted API? If yes, where (region) and for how long?
2) Are any prompts/outputs used to train or improve models?
3) Is there an auditable deletion workflow for prompts/outputs on request (we need documented SLAs)?
4) For Dedicated: please confirm that request/response data stays within our Dedicated tenancy and whether Redwood staff have access by default.
5) Can we enable customer-managed KMS?
6) Do you have a SOC 2 attestation and recent pen test summary we can share with procurement?

If you can get a one-page confirmation addressing the above, legal will be happy to accept and we can move to commercial. Also include any links to the Console settings where we can toggle logging/no-store.

Appreciate it 
Jared
Director of Product, Acme Health
jared.liu@acmehealth.com

Hi Jared 

Thanks  below is a concise, written confirmation you can share with procurement/legal. I also attached our SOC2 summary (redacted) and a one-pager. If anything needs to be more formalized (signed addendum), Marissa is looped on this thread to help.

Written confirmation (short):
- Persistence: Hosted API  Redwood retains request/response logs by default for 30 days for debugging/abuse monitoring. Prompts and outputs are not used to train models. If you require, we can configure no-store for your tenant which prevents request/response persistence in our control plane.
- Dedicated: Requests are served from your Dedicated tenancy. By default, request/response data is isolated to your tenancy and access by Redwood personnel is restricted to ops with just-in-time access and audit logging; we can further restrict access and set retention to 0 days for prompts/outputs as a contractual control.
- Private/VPC: No data leaves your environment unless explicitly configured.
- Data residency: We operate multiple regions (US, EU). Hosted customers can select region at provisioning; Dedicated deployments can be provisioned in customer-preferred region (we will confirm region-specific storage controls in contract).
- Deletion: We provide an auditable deletion workflow (API + Console) for requests and for associated persisted artifacts. Standard SLA for deletion request acknowledgement is 48 hours; full propagation depends on retention and backups  we can contract a more stringent SLA if required.
- Encryption & KMS: All persisted data is encrypted at rest. For Dedicated and Private, customer-managed KMS is supported; for Hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS option under enterprise terms.
- Auditing & logs: Audit logs are available via the Redwood Console and can be exported. Default audit log retention is 90 days; retention period is configurable in enterprise agreements.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II attestation and pen test summaries are available; see attached redacted SOC2_report_redacted.pdf and link to compliance folder.

Attachments: PII_handling_summary.pdf (one-pager), SOC2_report_redacted.pdf
Links: Console toggles are under Console -> Security -> Request Logging (we'll share a short gif in the technical deep-dive).

Next steps:
1) Marissa will coordinate a 30\u201345m technical call with our security engineer to walk through KMS setup and the deletion API.
2) If you want a Dedicated test environment in the EU, we'll generate a proposal and timeline (est. 3\u20135 business days to provision).
3) If procurement needs a signed addendum for logging/no-store, Marissa will prepare a draft.

Marissa / Neha  can you take point on scheduling the technical deep-dive and pulling the standard no-store addendum draft? Jared  what times next week look best for your security/infra folks?

Thanks,
Rishi
